flashcards.q: Why can a mypy --strict-clean function still crash at runtime on bad external data?
flashcards.a: Type hints are erased at runtime -- mypy checks static internal consistency assuming declared types are true, but nothing enforces that assumption against actual incoming data unless something explicitly validates (Pydantic, isinstance).

flashcards.q: Structural (Protocol) vs nominal (ABC) typing -- core distinction?
flashcards.a: Protocol: satisfied by having the right shape (methods/attrs), zero inheritance required -- matches Python's runtime duck typing. ABC: requires explicit inheritance, needed when you want shared implementation or a deliberate, non-accidental contract.

flashcards.q: Why must list[T] be invariant while Iterator[T] can be covariant?
flashcards.a: If list[Dog] were covariant with list[Animal], code holding the Animal-typed alias could .append(Cat()) into an actual list[Dog], smuggling a wrong subtype in. Iterator only produces T (no input position), so Iterator[Dog] safely substitutes for Iterator[Animal] with no way to insert a wrong type.

flashcards.q: Why is Callable[[Animal],None] a safe substitute for Callable[[Dog],None] (contravariance)?
flashcards.a: A function accepting any Animal can handle everything a Dog-only function can, and more -- every call site expecting to pass a Dog remains satisfied. The reverse (Dog-only function used where any Animal might appear) is unsafe. Function params are contravariant, return types are covariant, simultaneously.

flashcards.q: What problem does Pydantic solve that static type hints + mypy do not?
flashcards.a: Runtime enforcement -- Pydantic validates actual incoming data (API requests, config, LLM tool-call args) at a trust boundary, raising a structured ValidationError on mismatch. Mypy only checks internal code consistency assuming declared types are true; it can't verify external data.

flashcards.q: Pydantic v1 to v2 -- name the three real (non-cosmetic) API changes.
flashcards.a: Validator decorators (@validator -> @field_validator/@model_validator), config (class Config -> model_config=ConfigDict(...)), serialization (.dict()/.json() -> .model_dump()/.model_dump_json()) -- plus stricter default coercion behavior in v2, requiring manual review, not just find-replace.

flashcards.q: Why is pydantic-core (Rust) meaningfully faster than v1's pure-Python validation?
flashcards.a: v2 compiles type annotations once into a schema of composable Rust validators executed largely outside Python's per-field interpreter overhead. v1's per-field Python overhead compounds most on large, deeply-nested payloads -- exactly where the reported 5-50x speedup is largest.

flashcards.q: Why did Python 3.12 introduce native generic syntax (class Stack[T]:) when TypeVar already worked?
flashcards.a: Pre-3.12 generics needed a module-level TypeVar declared once and often reused across unrelated generic definitions, risking scoping ambiguity. PEP 695's syntax scopes T directly to the class/function definition, eliminating the boilerplate and reuse risk, and often auto-infers variance from usage.

flashcards.q: mypy rejects passing a list[Dog] variable to a param typed list[Animal], even though the function never mutates it. Fix?
flashcards.a: Change the parameter type to Sequence[Animal] (or Iterable[Animal]) -- the covariant, read-only supertype, correctly reflecting the function's read-only usage instead of over-specifying with invariant, mutation-permitting list.
